body:
Triage: lands in `domain:engine-core`; queued (`pm:queue`).

**Routing decision** (the decision this card was filed to get):

- **Route 3 — redact-on-read via `internal: true` + a purpose-built privileged accessor in `packages/objectql` (the `resolveSecret` pattern, named as the remedy by #7728 itself)** is the route this card takes. Rationale:
  1. It is the **only shape that covers the whole population**: redaction at the `sys_http_delivery` row layer catches both `WebhookSchema`-authored headers *and* `source: 'flow'` per-run interpolated headers — the half the card warns every other shape forgets.
  2. Route 2 (author-declared sensitive header names in `webhook.zod.ts` + `HttpConfigSchema`) both **under-covers** (misses the flow half by its own admission) and **expands the authorable spec surface** — a new declared key is a permanent maintenance obligation and would need the maintainer regardless. Not taken.
  3. Route 1 (`Field.secret()`) is rejected with measurements already on the card (orphan `sys_secret` row per delivery, boot-window fail-open on enqueue, per-tick decrypt).
- This is treated as a bug fix pulling the row back to the already-ruled posture of this family (#7799 / #7990 / #8114: credentials are not cleartext-readable at rest), not a contract expansion — the read surface narrows, nothing is accepted that was refused before.

**Cross-domain exception (designated by the triage seat):** the fix surface spans `packages/objectql` (accessor + `omitInternalFields` seam) and `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks` (`SqlHttpOutbox.claim()` rewired to the accessor; `sys_http_delivery` field marking). One PR, claimed by the **engine-core** seat; the claim comment must declare the full file surface and run the targeted in-flight check against `domain:services` claims (#7986 ①-f and #8081 are live in that lane; #8069 is adjacent).

Constraints carried from the card body are binding: no fail-closed weakening, no regression of #7799 / #8022 / #8114, and the `source: 'flow'` half must be shown covered in the PR's test evidence. If implementation finds the accessor route cannot hold (premise falsified), stop and report a fork — do not silently fall back to route 2, which re-enters maintainer territory.

Type: Bug.

## Targeted in-flight check — the exception path's one mandatory step

Ran against every **live** `domain:services` claim, reading each one's own declared file surface rather than inferring from titles:

| services card | state | declared surface | intersects? |

| **#7986** (this card's parent) | `pm:dispatched` | ①-a held `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/**` + `sys-webhook.object.ts` | ⭐ **released** — **PR #8114 MERGED 16:49:24Z**, verified on the PR itself. ①-f is `plugin-email` and its own card sequences it **behind** this one |

## Model rationale

**`claude-fable-5`, and the clause leaves no discretion.** Two independent prongs: the fix **adds a privileged accessor to `packages/objectql`** — new public face — and it **narrows the data-API read surface** on `sys_http_delivery.headers_json`. Either alone triggers the clause.

⚠️ **Known risk, recorded before the fact:** three consecutive `API Error: 529 Overloaded` kills took down the fable-tier dispatch on #7378 between ~17:0xZ and ~17:1xZ, and that card is parked in `pm:queue` awaiting fleet recovery. This dispatch is therefore **also the recovery probe**. ⛔ Downgrading the tier to route around an availability problem is not an option — an outage does not lower a correctness bar. If this one is killed the same way, it parks with the same provenance and both wait together.

Seat #6019. Triage's route-3 ruling and the card's binding constraints (⛔ no fail-closed weakening; ⛔ no regression of #7799 / #8022 / #8114; the `source: 'flow'` half must be **shown** covered) are carried into the dispatch verbatim and are not reopenable.

## Claim released — parked back to `pm:queue`. ⛔ Fleet outage, ⛔ not a verdict on the card.

Engine-core seat #6019, `session_014C8pAprWdmtecFsEprZax4`. `pm:dispatched` → `pm:queue`, assignee cleared, same label write as this comment. **Nothing was produced**: no branch, no commit, no partial diff — the card is exactly as triage left it, ruling and all.

### The canary result, which is now evidence rather than a hypothesis

This dispatch was **deliberately also the recovery probe** for #7378, which had been parked after three consecutive `API Error: 529 Overloaded` kills. It was killed the same way, before doing any work.

| model tier | dispatches this hour | 529 kills |
|---|---|---|
| **`claude-fable-5`** | 2 cards (#7378, #8118) | **4** |
| `opus` | 1 card (#8093) | **0** — still running |

Four kills across **two independent cards** at one tier, zero at another in the same window, is a much stronger reading than the 3-on-one-card that justified the first park. ⛔ The fable tier is shedding load; this is not something either card did.

### ⛔ What I did not do, and why it matters more than what I did

**I did not re-dispatch either card at a lower tier.** #8118 hits the fable clause on two independent prongs — it adds a **privileged accessor** to `packages/objectql` (new public face) and it **narrows** the data-API read surface on `sys_http_delivery.headers_json`. The clause carries no downward discretion.

⚠️ The temptation here is real and worth naming, because a future PM will feel it: this is a **security card** with a live cleartext-credential exposure, the fix is ruled, the surface is clear, and `opus` is demonstrably healthy. Routing around the outage would get it moving today. **It would also mean an availability problem silently lowered a correctness bar** — and the tier exists precisely because an error on a privileged-read accessor is the expensive kind. ⛔ An outage makes a card wait; it does not make it cheaper to get wrong.

### Restart condition — time-based now, because the probe already failed once

⛔ The previous restart condition ("re-dispatch once a fable-tier dispatch in this lane completes without a 529") is **superseded** — that probe has now been run and failed, and re-running it every patrol would just be a retry loop wearing a condition's clothing.

**Replacement:** hold both #8118 and #7378 for **at least one full patrol interval (~40 min)** before the next fable attempt, then dispatch **#8118 first** (it is the security card and outranks #7378 on the queue). If that attempt is killed again, park again, extend the hold, and **say so in the round report every time** — ⛔ silent retries are how a parked card becomes a forgotten one.

Everything about the card is unchanged and binding: triage's **route 3** ruling, ⛔ no fail-closed weakening, ⛔ no regression of #7799 / #8022 / #8114, the `source: 'flow'` half must be **shown** covered, and ⛔ a falsified accessor premise is a reported fork, never a quiet fall-back to route 2.

⚠️ For whoever picks this up: the targeted in-flight check was run at claim time and **passed** — #7986's hold on `plugin-webhooks/**` released when PR #8114 merged (16:49:24Z); #8081 and #8050 are disjoint. That reading is ~an hour old by the time this restarts and ⛔ must be re-run, not inherited.

## ⛔ BLOCKED on a maintainer action — the Fable 5 quota is exhausted. **Work is pushed and safe.**

Engine-core seat #6019, `session_014C8pAprWdmtecFsEprZax4`. `pm:dispatched` → **`pm:blocked`**, ⛔ assignee deliberately **kept**.

### The failure, and why it is a different class from this card's earlier ones

```
Agent terminated early due to an API error:
You've reached your Fable 5 limit. Run /usage-credits to continue or switch models.
```

⛔ **This is not the 529 fleet overload that parked this card and #7378 earlier.** That was transient and self-clearing. This is an **account quota** — it does not clear with time, and **only the maintainer can lift it**. Retrying is pointless and I am not going to spend wakeups doing it.

⛔ **And I cannot route around it by switching models.** This card hits the fable clause on two independent prongs — a **privileged accessor** on `packages/objectql` (new public face) and a **narrowing** of the data-API read surface. The clause has no downward discretion, and an exhausted budget is even less of a reason to lower a correctness bar than an outage was.

### ⭐ The early-push instruction did its job — nothing is lost

Four fable dispatches died before producing anything, so this dispatch carried an explicit *"push a commit as early as you can, even a WIP scaffold"*. **It worked.** `claude/issue-8118-delivery-headers-privileged-read` carries four real commits:

```
d23266555 test(service-messaging): pin the fail-closed fake engine's update() to the engine dispatch contract
e897847a8 fix(service-messaging): redact sys_http_delivery.headers_json on the generic read path;
          claim() recovers it via the privileged accessor
4778ce815 feat(objectql): resolveInternalField — batch privileged dereference for internal:true fields
c17e8677f wip(#8118): scaffold — delivery headers privileged read (route 3)
```

That is **route 3 substantially implemented**: the accessor exists, the redaction is in place, `claim()` is rewired through the accessor, and a fail-closed double is pinned. The dev died with `check:query-options-erasure` green and the type-debt re-measure mid-crash — i.e. **in the gate-running tail, not in the design**.

### ⛔ Why the label is `pm:blocked` and not `pm:queue`

Returning it to the queue would invite a fresh dev to **redo four commits of pushed work** — the #4551 double-implementation this repo pays for repeatedly. `pm:dispatched` would be equally untrue: no dev is in flight. `pm:blocked` is the only honest option, and the assignee stays so the branch has an owner.

**On unblock, resume — ⛔ do not re-dispatch from scratch.** The next dev inherits this branch, reads the four commits, and continues from the gate tail.

### ⚠️ Two things the resuming dev (and I) must re-check

1. **The surface is not what I declared.** My claim named `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks`; the work landed in **`service-messaging`**. That may be correct — but it means the cross-seat picture must be re-derived before any flip, and a `domain:services` declaration is likely owed. ⛔ Do not flip on my original declaration.
2. **The targeted in-flight check is stale.** It passed at 17:2xZ against #7986 / #8081 / #8050; that reading is over an hour old and ⛔ must be re-run, not inherited.

### Restart condition

**Maintainer restores Fable 5 capacity.** ⛔ No timer, no retry loop — there is nothing to poll. Named in every round report until it moves.

`domain:engine-core` seat (#6019), session `session_01RDTnVvsgA6cUZ4xFVtPZRy`. Seat taken ~04:3xZ. `pm:blocked` **stays**, ⛔ assignee stays, ⛔ branch untouched — but the reason has changed and the honest thing is to say which reason is now load-bearing.

### The restart condition is met

The blocking condition was *"maintainer restores Fable 5 capacity"*. **It is restored** — verified with the read-only probe §5.12 prescribes (no tools, no branch, no claim) before I claimed anything, and three fable-tier cards from this lane's wall have already been implemented this shift (#8215 **landed** on `origin/main` @ `4b0ebdb`; #7501 and #7589 are in review). ⛔ The tier classification for this card is unchanged and not reopened: a privileged accessor on `packages/objectql` plus a narrowing of the data-API read surface, two independent prongs, no downward discretion.

**① The declared surface was wrong, and the correction is bigger than "not plugin-webhooks".** Measured from the four commits themselves (`c17e8677^..d232665`, control: exactly 4 commits in range) — ⛔ not from the claim, and ⛔ not from a merge-base diff, which on this branch returns 734 commits and a whole-repo file list and is therefore useless:

The work splits cleanly by commit — `4778ce81` is the objectql accessor, `e897847a` + `d2326655` are the service-messaging half — so a cross-seat declaration here can offer a genuinely separable commit rather than a promise.

**② ⛔ NEW HOLD — `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` collides with an in-flight card in this very lane.** PR #8327 (#7589, the dotted-projection refusal) is open on `engine.ts` right now. This is a **hard same-file serial**, and it is the exact shape §4 of the seat post was written about: #8327 does not merely add a check, it **DELETES** the head-only `known.has(head)` filter and the false populate comment. A card that removes something has a range nobody can infer from the name of what it added — which is how this seat landed a merge conflict in a block it had "cleared" as 158 lines apart.

⛔ I am therefore **not** dispatching this alongside #8327, and ⛔ not clearing it by distance. **#8118 resumes once #8327 has landed on `origin/main`**, at which point the resuming dev merges main into this branch and re-prices the accessor seam against the *merged* text.

### For the resuming dev, so the restart stays cheap

⭐ **Resume, ⛔ do not re-dispatch.** Four real commits implement route 3 substantially — the accessor exists, redaction is in place, `claim()` is rewired through it, and a fail-closed double is pinned. The dev died in the **gate tail**, not the design. ⛔ Do not re-run the original dispatch, ⛔ do not create a new worktree from scratch, ⛔ do not touch the assignee or the claim: read the four commits hunk by hunk and continue from the gate tail.

⚠️ The branch is behind `main` and the base has moved a great deal (including #8215 landing in `rule-validator.ts` and, shortly, #8327 in `engine.ts`). A merge with main is the **first** step, not the last.

Everything binding stays binding: triage's **route 3** ruling, ⛔ no fail-closed weakening, ⛔ no regression of #7799 / #8022 / #8114, the `source: 'flow'` half must be **shown** covered, and ⛔ a falsified accessor premise is a reported fork, never a quiet fall-back to route 2.

⚠️ The targeted in-flight check must be re-run **again** at resume time — mine is being recorded now and will itself be stale by then. Current reading: `domain:services` has #8081 and #7986 `pm:dispatched`; #8149 (`sys_email.headers_json`) is explicitly sequenced **behind** whatever this card lands and must not be decided separately.
